turns.query: Screen original Form N-MFP3 accessions with 2025 report dates and report-date net assets of at least $10 billion. Within each accession's report-date calendar month, order its reported liquidity observations by date and form consecutive steps. Retain steps whose weekly-liquid-asset amount and reported fraction are both positive at both endpoints. Rank by the most negative ending-minus-starting weekly-liquid-assets fraction, breaking a tie by earlier ending date, series name and accession. Report the eligible accession and step counts; selected accession, series, report date and net assets; step dates; both weekly-liquid-asset amounts and fractions; and decline-magnitude margin over the runner-up. Explain the selected liquidity signal.

For the accession and ending date selected above, aggregate all reported share-class flow rows on that exact date. Report the contributing row count, gross subscriptions, gross redemptions, and net outflow, redemptions minus subscriptions, divided by report-date net assets. Also report net outflow divided by the turn-1 decline in weekly liquid assets. Explain whether the two dollar movements reconcile.

Bracket the selected liquidity-step ending date with the immediately prior and immediately following CFTC report dates for the futures-only 3-month SOFR contract code 134741. For each endpoint calculate leveraged-money long minus short contracts. Report both dates, both net positions, their change, both open-interest levels and the open-interest change. Explain what this market-positioning overlay does and does not establish about the fund event.

Decompose the turn-1 dollar change in weekly liquid assets. At both step endpoints report daily liquid assets; weekly liquid assets minus daily liquid assets is the other component. Compute the ending-minus-starting change in each component and report their summed change minus the reported weekly-liquid-assets change. Explain which component drives the drawdown and the scope of this additive bridge.
